svg.title: Protest, Civil Rights & Nuclear Paranoia in Post-War Britain (1958–1983)
svg.desc: KS3 GIS historical atlas map of Great Britain (England, Wales, and Scotland) showing landmark post-war protest, civil rights, and Cold War nuclear sites: the Easter 1958 52-mile CND London-to-Aldermaston March, the 1963 Bristol Omnibus Boycott, the 1961 York Cold War Royal Observer Corps Bunker, Whitehall and the 1980 Protect and Survive booklet, and the 1981–83 RAF Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp.

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: RIGHTS & POST-WAR BRITAIN
Protest, Civil Rights & Nuclear Paranoia in Britain (1958–1983)
Post-war Britons reshaped democracy from below—defeating racial “colour bars” in Bristol (1963) and challenging nuclear weapons.
While officials staffed secret ROC bunkers and issued Protect and Survive (1980), CND and Greenham Common women mobilised mass protest.
